title: Cubical structures on rigidified invertible modules
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $p:G\to S$ be a commutative group scheme with identity $e$: its addition, inverse and identity are $S$-morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_G$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] with rigidification $r:e^*L\simeq\mathcal O_S$. All pullbacks below are tensor inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback], and tensor products are sheaf tensor products over the structure sheaf of the indicated scheme [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. On $G^3=G\times_SG\times_SG$ [def-pc-fibre-product], write $m_I$ for the sum of coordinates indexed by $I\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$, with $m_\varnothing=e\circ p_3$, where $p_3:G^3\to S$ is the structure map. Put
$$\Theta_3(L)=m_{123}^*L\otimes m_1^*L\otimes m_2^*L\otimes m_3^*L\otimes(m_{12}^*L)^{-1}\otimes(m_{13}^*L)^{-1}\otimes(m_{23}^*L)^{-1}\otimes(m_\varnothing^*L)^{-1}.$$
The inverse of an invertible module is its dual $\mathcal Hom(L,\mathcal O_G)$. A cubical structure compatible with $r$ is a nowhere vanishing section $\tau:\mathcal O_{G^3}\simeq\Theta_3(L)$, invariant under permutations of the three coordinates, whose restriction when any coordinate is $e$ is the unit section under the cancellations induced by $r$, and satisfying the cocycle identity on $G^4$:
$$\tau(x,y,z)\otimes\tau(x+y,w,z)=\tau(y,w,z)\otimes\tau(x,y+w,z).$$
Here evaluation at $(x,y,z)$ denotes pullback along the indicated coordinate-sum map, and the equality uses the canonical identification of the tensor products after cancelling equal line factors. Thus it is an identity of sections over $G^4$, equivalently after every base change and every quadruple of generalized points. A cubical rigidified line is $(L,r,\tau)$. Its isomorphisms are invertible-module isomorphisms preserving $r$ and carrying $\tau$ to the other cube section under $\Theta_3$. For a homomorphism $h:G'\to G$ of commutative group schemes over $S$, pullback of $(L,r,\tau)$ means $(h^*L,r',(h^3)^*\tau)$: here $r'$ is $e_{G'}^*h^*L\simeq e_G^*L\xrightarrow{r}\mathcal O_S$, and the cube section is read through $\Theta_3(h^*L)\simeq(h^3)^*\Theta_3(L)$. Restriction to a subscheme $S'\hookrightarrow S$ means the same termwise base change to $G\times_S S'$.
